endorsements.quote: At a minimum, this should include independent evaluation of companion chatbots using standardized youth crisis scenarios, red-team testing by external auditors with clinical and developmental expertise, longitudinal assessment of safety performance across major system updates, and verification that crisis responses and referrals are appropriate to the user's jurisdiction and language.

At a minimum, this should include independent evaluation of companion chatbots using standardized youth crisis scenarios, red-team testing by external auditors with clinical and developmental expertise, longitudinal assessment of safety performance across major system updates, and verification that crisis responses and referrals are appropriate to the user's jurisdiction and language.

These audits should assess whether systems reliably recognize suicide risk and other acute warning signs, provide active and context-appropriate crisis guidance, escalate appropriately to human or emergency support, and maintain acceptable performance across jurisdictions, languages, and successive product iterations [ 7 , 11 ].
Regulators should also require transparent reporting of crisis-response performance and re-certification after major system changes.

Specifically, current frameworks should be revised to require independent behavioral audits based on standardized youth crisis scenarios, explicit failure thresholds for unsafe or non-escalating responses, transparent public reporting of crisis-response performance, and mandatory re-evaluation after major system updates [ 7 , 11 ].

unlisted_practices: Regulators should require independent behavioral audits of companion chatbots based on standardized youth crisis scenarios.
Regulators should require explicit failure thresholds for unsafe or non-escalating chatbot responses.
Regulators should require re-certification of companion chatbots after major system changes.
Researchers should prioritize cross-jurisdictional and cross-linguistic evaluation and longitudinal assessment of chatbot safety across repeated interactions and major updates.
Regulators should not rely on disclosure of artificiality alone as a safeguard for adolescent users.
